profiles.meeting_scenario: Two weeks after a major Gulf Coast hurricane, a mid-sized Texas city's Disaster Recovery Office is holding a coordination meeting with a nonprofit coalition partner that is staffing hotel and shelter-based case management for incoming low-income evacuees. The city has just received a limited tranche of short-term housing assistance funds and needs to align handoffs from nonprofit case managers into the municipal housing referral queue. The agenda is to confirm which households should appear on the shared tracking list, what materials accompany each handoff, when Friday status updates will be submitted, and how both sides will describe progress to the wider interagency group. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the weekly interface between frontline case management and the city's housing placement team.

members.name: Elena Ruiz
members.expertise: Emergency housing operations, interagency reporting, public fund compliance, shelter-to-housing transitions
members.background: Elena works in the city's Disaster Recovery Office and previously managed rapid rehousing reporting for HUD-funded programs; during disasters she translates field information into auditable housing referrals and mayor's office briefings.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the city's new hurricane housing funds from being flagged for weak documentation, reduce duplicate names entering the housing queue, and produce a clean weekly status update that makes the city's coordination effort look controlled.
hidden_assumptions: An 'active case' is a household that still requires city-side action within the current weekly housing pipeline, not simply ongoing contact from a case manager.
The 'master list' means the city's deduplicated nightly export that merges shelter records, 211 referrals, and prior housing placements into one operational queue.
An 'intake packet' should already include the consent forms and eligibility documents the city needs to move a household directly into referral review.
A household is 'ready for housing referral' only once core verification items are attached, because the city should not open a formal placement slot for incomplete files.

members.name: Marcus Lee
members.expertise: Disaster case management, volunteer coordination, hotel and shelter intake workflows, survivor navigation across benefits systems
members.background: Marcus leads a coalition of nonprofits that placed rotating case managers in hotels and shelters after the storm; his team focuses on rapid engagement, basic needs, and helping evacuees navigate FEMA and local services before documentation is fully assembled.
members.private_state: He wants to keep families visible in the system before they disappear from hotels, avoid slowing staff down with paperwork too early, and show partner agencies that the coalition is successfully moving households toward longer-term help.
hidden_assumptions: An 'active case' is any household his staff is still checking in with because the situation remains unstable, even if no immediate city action is pending this week.
The 'master list' is the shared coalition spreadsheet circulated at VOAD calls, since that is the field-facing source everyone actually updates during the day.
The 'intake packet' is the basic frontline packet used at shelters and hotels—demographics, immediate needs, release, and notes—with specialized eligibility documents gathered later.

A case is 'ready for housing referral' once a case manager has confirmed homelessness risk and immediate barriers, because paperwork can be completed during referral follow-up without losing momentum.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to report the number of 'active cases' needing follow-up this week.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means households that still require a city housing action or pending municipal review in the current reporting cycle.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means households still receiving ongoing check-ins or navigation help from nonprofit case managers, even if no city-side step is imminent.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In disaster response, 'active case' sounds like routine case-management language, so each assumes the other is using the standard meaning from their own workflow and the conversation moves on to counts rather than definitions.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to updating 'the master list' before the interagency briefing.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the city's nightly deduplicated export stored in SharePoint and used for official housing queue management.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the coalition's Google Sheet maintained during daily field operations and circulated on volunteer-agency calls.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There are multiple widely used tracking artifacts and both are informally called the master list; because each list overlaps in purpose and some households appear on both, surface agreement feels natural.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that each handoff will include the 'intake packet.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the packet includes signed releases, FEMA correspondence, income or zero-income attestation, ID if available, and the city eligibility checklist.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the packet includes only the frontline shelter/hotel intake forms, immediate-needs notes, and whatever consent was gathered at first contact.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each side sees its own packet as the obvious default bundle attached to a handoff, and neither expects a coordination meeting to revisit what feels like established paperwork terminology.

misalignment_points.topic: When a case is 'ready for housing referral'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to send over households that are 'ready for housing referral' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready' means the case can enter formal municipal review immediately because documentation is sufficient to assign scarce housing funds without rework.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready' means the household has been screened as likely eligible and urgent enough that the city should start engaging while missing documents are chased afterward.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are oriented toward helping households move faster, so 'ready' sounds like a shared practical threshold even though one uses an administrative sufficiency standard and the other uses a field-triage standard.

What I need from Marcus is a manageable Friday handoff into the city's deduplicated queue so we can show leadership that the process is controlled.
